correctness.rationale: For each nonabsorbing mutant mask of P3, the precisely stated Bd or dB parent-replacement probabilities define a finite absorbing Markov chain. The 6-state Dirichlet solution yields explicit rational fixation probabilities for center/end r-site placements. Subtracting factors differences into +2(r−s)P(r,s)/positive and −2(r−s)/[9(r+1)(s+1)], with every coefficient of P positive for r,s>0; r=s ties. Independently constructed exact Fraction first-step elimination reproduces the r=2,s=1 values 11/24 vs 25/63 for Bd and 1/3 vs 10/27 for dB. This finite diagnostic supports, but does not replace, the general symbolic factorization.
residual_risks: No formal theorem prover certification; bounded finite checks not all-size proofs.

value.rationale: The smallest path with inequivalent habitat positions exhibits an across-update-rule reversal in optimal placement for every positive mutant-only fecundity contrast. Position-dependent environmental selection and update-order sensitivity are natural evolutionary-graph questions; a complete sharp universal three-site classification is nontrivial despite tiny graph size, because it distinguishes placement from initial-mutant-site effects.
